page.layout: One printed page: one column of running text, with the running head above it and the page number at the top right. Catchword "quod" at the lower right, gathering signature "H" at the lower left. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: ternas in aere esse sitas, non imus inficias. Nam in quibuscunq; locis (teste Cornelio Celso, libr. primo de Re medica) modo calor adest, modo frigus, pestilentia fit. Quod sane septentrionales monticolæ satis experiuntur. Quæ postmodum his subiungit Fernelius, nimirum pestilentium morborum causam esse cœcam & occultam, & eam tamen esse inquinatum aerem, non recte inter se cohærere videntur. Nam una & eadem causa non potest simul esse, & euidens, & occulta. At aër externa est causa, & propterea euidens. Quod sane haud negare queunt Ferneliani. Nam ipsorum doctor libro de Morborum causis, externas causas & procatharticas euidentes appellat: Vbi quoq; ex ipso euidentium genere aerem nos circumstantem esse tradit. In nos (forte) retorquebunt Fernelij sectatores (quos non pauci, & præsertim grammaticales medicos fore scio) non ipsum aerem nobis circumfusum, sed eius inquinamentum, malignāque qualitatem, quæ abdita est, pestis causam esse. At aeris labem esse occultam & ignotam naturalis scientiæ imperitis libenter concedemus, sed hanc esse internam morbi causam constanter negabimus. Id deniq;

page.notes: Page is one continuous paragraph carried over from the previous page. The running head "CAVSAS, PROGYMNASMATA." is printed in small capitals with the page number 115 at the top right. Long s has been normalised to s throughout. Line-end hyphens in "circum-fusum", "libe-nter" and "maligna-que" were joined; "morbi" is split across lines without a printed hyphen and is written whole. The text "retorquebunt" and "pauci" are read from the scan; "aër" and "aerem" are printed with the diaeresis as shown. The page ends mid-word with "deniq;" followed by the catchword "quod".
